threat_event: Ransomware delivered by a phishing email or malicious attachment encrypts the store computers, the packaging workstation, and the synced shared drive, stopping dispensing at the counter
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No phishing training; antivirus only, with alerts in business hours; flat store network; same local administrator password on every computer; backup never restore-tested
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-02; SYS-03; SYS-05; SYS-07; BP-01; BP-05
likelihood_basis: EV-041 (privacy video only; no phishing training); EV-016 (antivirus alerts in business hours only); EV-015 (no EDR in MSP services); EV-017 (one staff network); EV-018 (no restore jobs)
existing_controls: MFA on email; MSP patching and antivirus; firewall; PMS is vendor-hosted
treatment_plan: Annual training plus quarterly phishing simulations; MSP-managed endpoint detection and response (EDR) with alert monitoring; unique local administrator passwords; 90-day immutable backup versions; quarterly restore tests; written downtime and diversion procedure (P08)

threat_event: Data theft during a ransomware attack (double extortion) exposes delivery logs, ALF medication lists, and downloaded faxes, leading to a reportable breach of several thousand patients
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: PHI in the shared drive (monthly delivery log exports since 2021) and in download folders on unencrypted desktops; no inventory of where ePHI lives; no alerting on large uploads
likelihood_basis: EV-010 (delivery log exports since 2021 in the shared drive); EV-048 (downloaded faxes on the counter desktops); EV-014 (desktops unencrypted); EV-006 (no download or forwarding alerts); EV-045 (records for about 11,500 individuals)
treatment_plan: ePHI inventory; delete delivery log exports older than the retention need; weekly clean-up of download folders; suite alerts for mass download and new forwarding rules; EDR (R-001)

threat_event: Someone in the store uses an open or password-only PMS session to view, enter, or change prescriptions under another person's name
threat_source: Workforce member or intruder on a store computer
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: In-store PMS sign-in is password only; 60-minute idle timeout; the 3 counter desktops run under one shared operating system account that never locks
likelihood_basis: EV-003 (in-store sign-in password only; 60-minute timeout); EV-013 (shared counter account excluded from screen lock); EV-053 (staff work under the last person's session)
treatment_plan: 15-minute PMS timeout with quick re-sign-in; vendor second-factor option for in-store sign-in; individual desktop accounts with screen lock

threat_event: Former workforce member signs in to the PMS, email, or delivery app after leaving
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Removal depends on memory; a former technician's PMS and email accounts stayed active about 11 weeks (disabled 2026-07-14)
likelihood_basis: EV-001 (April 2026 termination); EV-052 (accounts active about 11 weeks); EV-048 (accounts removed when remembered)
existing_controls: Named accounts; MFA on email tied to the user's phone
treatment_plan: Last-day checklist (PMS, email, fax portal, delivery app, MSP tool, keys, alarm code); monthly account reconciliation by the Store Manager

threat_event: Shared-drive files or the packaging workstation cannot be restored after deletion, corruption, or encryption
threat_source: Backup misconfiguration or sync of damaged files
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 30 days of versions; not immutable; one MSP administrator account without MFA; never restore-tested
likelihood_basis: EV-018 (30-day versions; not immutable; no restore jobs); EV-053 (backup console password only)
treatment_plan: First restore test of a shared-drive folder and a full rebuild of the packaging workstation from its image; 90-day immutable versions; MFA on the console; quarterly tests recorded

threat_event: A non-pharmacist annotates or alters a dispensed controlled substance prescription record
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: The permission to alter controlled substance records had been given to the Lead Pharmacy Technician and the Store Manager in 2019 to fix claim errors
likelihood_basis: EV-055 (alteration permission held by 2 non-pharmacists since 2019); EV-056 (12-month audit trail review)
existing_controls: PMS audit trail of every alteration
treatment_plan: Permission removed from both on 2026-07-17; pharmacist-owner reviewed the 12-month audit trail of alterations (no changes to drug, quantity, or patient); role check added to the quarterly review

threat_event: Theft of an unencrypted desktop exposes downloaded faxes and reports
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 5 desktops unencrypted; downloaded faxes and reports in their download folders
likelihood_basis: EV-014 (5 desktops unencrypted); EV-048 (downloaded faxes in download folders); EV-047 (keyed entry; alarm; cameras)
existing_controls: Store locked after hours; monitored alarm; cameras
treatment_plan: MSP enables full-disk encryption on all 5 desktops and reports status monthly

threat_event: Attacker enters through the packaging vendor's always-on remote connection or exploits the unsupported packaging workstation and moves to the store desktops
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Unsupported operating system without patches or antivirus; always-on vendor connection with a shared vendor password; shared packaging login; same network as the desktops; no BAA with the equipment vendor
likelihood_basis: EV-012 (unsupported operating system; excluded from patching and antivirus); EV-020 (always-on vendor connection; shared password and login); EV-017 (same network as the desktops); EV-021 (no BAA with the equipment vendor)
existing_controls: Firewall blocks unsolicited inbound traffic; vendor tool connects outbound only
treatment_plan: Separate network segment for SYS-05; vendor access only on request with a session log and named vendor accounts; BAA with the equipment vendor; supported controller at the next equipment refresh, written into the service contract

threat_event: PMS vendor outage longer than the 4-hour RTO
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No written downtime procedure; single SaaS dependency for profiles, e-prescriptions, claims, and labels
likelihood_basis: EV-038 (no downtime procedure); EV-023 (vendor RTO 4 hours); EV-022 (no recovery figures in the agreement)
treatment_plan: Downtime card at each station (paper log, emergency refills under Fla. Stat. 465.0275(1), PDMP outage rule, partner pharmacy transfers); confirm vendor RTO and RPO in the contract

threat_event: Internet outage stops access to the PMS, phones, and fax
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One internet line; no failover; VoIP phones on the same line
likelihood_basis: EV-031 (one internet line, no failover)
treatment_plan: MSP installs a cellular failover router; phone hotspot as a stopgap

threat_event: An EPCS security event (unauthorized access, alteration, or interference) is missed and not reported to DEA and the PMS vendor within one business day
threat_source: Workforce member or intruder; process failure
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: The daily EPCS audit report is generated but never opened; no reporting procedure
likelihood_basis: EV-004 (daily EPCS reports unopened); EV-059 (reports never opened before 2026-07-21); EV-038 (no reporting procedure)
existing_controls: PMS generates the report and keeps the audit trail
treatment_plan: Pharmacist on duty reviews the report each business day and initials the log; POL-03 sets the one-business-day DEA and vendor report

threat_event: Proof-of-delivery app vendor exposes or reuses patient names, addresses, and prescription numbers
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Free-tier app with no BAA and unknown retention; one shared driver account reused since 2025
likelihood_basis: EV-009 (free tier; no BAA; retention not stated); EV-048 (one driver login reused since 2025)
treatment_plan: BAA on a paid plan or replace with an app that signs one; named driver account; delete data older than 90 days

threat_event: Compromise of the MSP's remote management tool gives attackers access to every store computer
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: MSP tool has administrator access to all computers; no review of MSP security practices
likelihood_basis: EV-028 (remote tool reaches every computer; no incident notice term); EV-051 (MSP states MFA on its console, no evidence supplied)
existing_controls: BAA with the MSP; MSP states its console uses MFA (not evidenced)
treatment_plan: Annual MSP security review (questionnaire and evidence of MFA, technician list, subcontractors); 24-hour incident notice and a recovery time commitment in the next contract

threat_event: Someone other than the certificate holder uses the CSOS private key to sign Schedule II orders
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: The Store Manager placed Schedule II orders with the owner's CSOS certificate on the owner's laptop; certificate password saved in the browser
likelihood_basis: EV-057 (Store Manager used the owner's certificate; password saved in the browser); EV-035 (one certificate holder)
existing_controls: Laptop encrypted; orders received and counted by a second person
treatment_plan: Certificate revoked on 2026-07-17 and replaced on 2026-08-03 (paper DEA order forms in between); password no longer saved; the Store Manager applies for a separate certificate under a power of attorney (21 CFR 1311.25(a))

threat_event: OCR enforcement after a complaint or breach because the pharmacy never did a risk analysis or adopted policies
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No risk analysis before 2026; policy binder never adopted; no device or ePHI inventory
likelihood_basis: EV-039 (2022 vendor checklist only); EV-038 (binder never adopted); EV-012 (device list has computers only)
treatment_plan: Adopt P06 policies; annual risk analysis update; device and ePHI inventory; keep 12 months of evidence of recognized security practices

threat_event: Staff do not recognize or report an incident, so breach and DEA clocks are missed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No incident plan; no reporting channel; a misdirected fax in March 2026 was never assessed or logged
likelihood_basis: EV-038 (no incident plan or log); EV-053 (March 2026 misdirected fax not assessed); EV-041 (training at hire only)
treatment_plan: POL-03 and the P08 runbook; reporting card at every station; annual training; tabletop exercise

threat_event: Fax or email with PHI sent to the wrong recipient or without encryption
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No verification step for new fax numbers; outside email encrypted only when the sender chooses it (4 of 10 ALF emails were not)
likelihood_basis: EV-051 (no second check for new fax numbers); EV-061 (4 of 10 ALF emails unencrypted); EV-011 (encryption only when the sender chooses it)
treatment_plan: Saved contacts for prescribers and the ALFs; automatic encryption rule for outside email with PHI; double-check rule in training

threat_event: Hurricane closes the store for several days
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No contingency plan; one location; no generator
likelihood_basis: EV-038 (no contingency plan); EV-047 (one storefront; no generator)
existing_controls: PMS reachable from any location; laptops encrypted
treatment_plan: Hurricane checklist: pre-storm 30-day refills where a state of emergency allows (Fla. Stat. 465.0275(2)); ALF packs built a week ahead; partner pharmacy arrangement; patient notice script

threat_event: The PMS controlled substance risk score leads to an unjustified refusal or delay, or treats patients differently by sex or age
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Switched on by a vendor release without review; uses age and sex as inputs; technicians see the flag and tell patients; no local testing
likelihood_basis: EV-025 (switched on by default; release notes unread); EV-026 (age and sex among the inputs); EV-049 (flag visible to all staff)
treatment_plan: Score visible to pharmacists only; pharmacist documents independent judgment; vendor asked to explain or remove the sex input; quarterly bias check (see P10)

threat_event: Claims switch outage delays real-time claims
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single switch through the PMS vendor
likelihood_basis: EV-022 (one claims switch through the PMS vendor); EV-051 (past switch outages lasted hours); EV-044 (cash reserve)
existing_controls: PBM help desks; downtime log for later submission
treatment_plan: Accepted: switch outages historically last hours; urgent prescriptions are dispensed and billed after recovery; cash reserve covers about 3 weeks

threat_event: Lost or stolen laptop or delivery phone exposes PHI
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Laptops and the delivery phone leave the store
likelihood_basis: EV-014 (laptops and phone encrypted; remote wipe)
existing_controls: Laptops encrypted; phone encrypted with passcode; MSP and the phone platform can wipe
treatment_plan: Accepted: PHI encrypted consistent with HHS guidance is not unsecured PHI (45 CFR 164.402); residual risk Low

threat_event: Business email compromise of a staff mailbox exposes ALF lists and prescriber correspondence
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: MFA in place, but staff approve push prompts without checking; no phishing training
likelihood_basis: EV-051 (staff approve push prompts without checking); EV-006 (number matching off); EV-041 (no phishing training)
treatment_plan: Switch MFA to number matching; training (R-001); block automatic external forwarding

threat_event: Attacker who controls one store computer reuses the shared local administrator password to take over every desktop and the packaging workstation
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: The MSP set the same local administrator password on all 5 desktops and the packaging workstation in 2021 (found in P07 testing)
likelihood_basis: EV-IA-5 (shared local administrator password found in P07 testing)
treatment_plan: MSP sets a unique, rotated local administrator password on every computer with its password management tool; equipment vendor changes the packaging workstation password
